story.headline: SK Hynix Reports Record Q3 Revenue and Operating Profit Driven by AI Demand
story.summary: SK Hynix announced plans to return over $22 billion in dividends and $15 billion in buybacks to shareholders following a record quarter. The capital return builds upon the South Korean memory maker's previous multibillion-dollar buyback programs driven by strong AI demand.

draft.body:
On October 28, 2026, South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix announced record third-quarter financial results, driven by relentless enterprise demand for high-bandwidth memory in artificial intelligence accelerators. The company surpassed 100 trillion won in quarterly sales for the first time in its history and announced a comprehensive shareholder return program worth approximately 100 trillion won (about $75 billion) for fiscal year 2026.

According to the [SK hynix Newsroom earnings announcement](https://news.skhynix.com/en/q3-2026-business-results/), consolidated revenue for the third quarter reached 104.6155 trillion won, climbing 32 percent from the second quarter and 328 percent from the same period a year earlier. Operating profit hit an all-time high of 83.3338 trillion won, representing an operating profit margin of 80 percent, while net profit came in at 39.7756 trillion won.

## Record Q3 Earnings and Cash Accumulation

The operating results exceeded market expectations across major benchmarks. Operating profit increased by 38 percent quarter-over-quarter from 60.5426 trillion won in the second quarter of 2026, and jumped 632 percent from 11.3834 trillion won in the third quarter of 2025. As reported by [Channel NewsAsia](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/sk-hynix-unveils-75-billion-shareholder-return-plan-after-posting-record-profit-6498106), the 83.33 trillion won operating profit cleared the 76.7 trillion won consensus estimate compiled by LSEG SmartEstimate. Following the release, the company's shares gained as much as 9.4 percent in morning trading in Seoul.

The surge in memory average selling prices drove significant cash generation. By the end of the third quarter, SK Hynix held 114.5 trillion won in cash and cash equivalents, reflecting a quarterly increase of 26.5 trillion won. Simultaneously, total borrowings dropped by 2.8 trillion won to 15.8 trillion won, lifting the company's net cash position to 98.7 trillion won.

[[FIG1]]

## Shareholder Returns and the Solidigm IPO Cancellation

Buoyed by its cash expansion, SK Hynix finalized an aggressive capital return strategy intended to fulfill its commitment to distribute at least 50 percent of free cash flow to shareholders. The plan includes at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and at least 60 trillion won in share repurchases and cancellations across fiscal year 2026, as detailed by [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10917003). A 40 trillion won share buyback authorized in August was completed in late October, with those shares slated for cancellation.

The board of directors approved a third-quarter cash dividend of 14 trillion won, translating to 20,000 won per share. This payout consists of a standard operational dividend of 10,000 won alongside a 10,000 won special dividend funded by returns realized from the company's strategic investment in Japanese memory producer Kioxia. The board also authorized a separate 20 trillion won share repurchase, of which 10 trillion won will be canceled for shareholder returns, while the remaining 10 trillion won is allocated toward employee compensation.

During the earnings briefing, SK Hynix Chief Executive Officer Kwak Noh-Jung revealed that the company has formally terminated its review of an initial public offering for Solidigm. The IPO had originally been considered to raise external funds for Solidigm fab expansions, but executive management concluded that current capital market conditions meant an offering would not achieve the desired strategic objectives.

[[FIG2]]

## HBM4 Acceleration and Fab Expansion Plans

The earnings surge was anchored by higher shipments across advanced DRAM and NAND categories. Commercial deliveries of HBM4 began in earnest during the third quarter, while server DDR5 sales increased substantially, according to [Korea JoongAng Daily](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/sk-hynixs-q3-operating-profit-surges-more-than-sevenfold-to-record-628b-beating-forecasts/12941760). In the NAND business, sales of 321-layer TLC eSSDs expanded, and high-value-added products for data centers continued to grow across the board.

SK Hynix stated that HBM4 will surpass previous-generation HBM3E in both shipment volume and total revenue during the fourth quarter of 2026, establishing itself as the company's primary high-bandwidth memory product. To support the ramp, the chipmaker is pushing its M15X production line to maximum capacity before the end of the year. Production is also pivoting toward 10nm-class sixth-generation (1c) process nodes, with expanded shipments of server DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM modules tailored for AI clusters. In NAND, the 321-layer process will account for more than half of domestic production capacity in the fourth quarter.

Long-term fabrication investments will see additional resources next year. The first phase of SK Hynix's mega-fab campus in Yongin is scheduled to begin full-scale manufacturing in 2027, with investment expected to increase significantly for equipment for advanced chipmaking processes and infrastructure.

[[FIG3]]

## Structural Supply Deficits Projected Through 2030

Addressing analyst concerns regarding potential corrections in AI capital expenditures, SK Hynix projected that the supply deficit across cutting-edge memory will persist until 2030. According to statements cited by [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20261028/0d63cf80c3c544bba860b79a2fd1e243/c.html), the market is entering a second phase where spending is broadening from a handful of hyper-scalers to general enterprise customers and sovereign AI initiatives. According to SK Hynix's analysis of the virtuous cycle of AI adoption, enterprise automation in customer support, code generation, and search indexing has established self-sustaining software revenues that justify ongoing hardware outlays.

The company stated that customer demand for HBM continues to outstrip total manufacturing capability by a factor of two, leaving its HBM and DRAM chips sold out until 2029. To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility and solidify its growth foundation, SK Hynix has signed long-term agreements with 14 major customers, including leading cloud infrastructure providers. These long-term agreements secure firm commitments for more than 50 percent of the company's planned production volume across 2027 and 2028, incorporating flexible pricing collars that ensure baseline profitability while adjusting to shifting macroeconomic conditions.

faq.q: What were SK Hynix's third-quarter 2026 financial highlights?
faq.a: SK Hynix reported record revenue of 104.62 trillion won, an operating profit of 83.33 trillion won with an 80% operating margin, and a net profit of 39.78 trillion won.

faq.q: How much capital is SK Hynix returning to shareholders?
faq.a: The company announced an annual capital return plan of approximately 100 trillion won ($75 billion) for 2026, comprising at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and at least 60 trillion won in share repurchases and cancellations.

faq.q: Why was the Solidigm IPO canceled?
faq.a: CEO Kwak Noh-Jung stated that after reviewing recent financial market conditions, management determined that proceeding with an IPO was no longer the most effective mechanism to expand manufacturing capacity or maximize shareholder value.

faq.q: How long does SK Hynix expect the AI memory shortage to last?
faq.a: SK Hynix forecasts that high-end memory supply will lag behind demand through 2030, citing extreme technical manufacturing hurdles and prolonged fab construction lead times.
